q: 'Shunting' in railway operations means:

options.A: Running of a train through a station without stopping
options.C: Washing of coaches in a yard
options.D: The movement of coaches and wagons within station limits for forming, breaking up or placing trains

e: Shunting is the movement of coaches and wagons within station limits for forming, breaking up or placing trains.

q: 'Interlocking' in railway signalling is an arrangement under which:

options.B: A signal cannot be taken 'off' unless the points are correctly set and locked for the route, so that conflicting movements cannot be authorised
options.C: Level crossing gates are locked during the night
options.D: Coaches are locked together by vacuum pipes

e: Interlocking is an arrangement under which a signal cannot be taken off unless the points are correctly set and locked for the route, preventing conflicting movements.

q: Under the Absolute Block System of train working:

options.A: Only one train is allowed to be in a block section between two block stations at a time
options.B: Several trains can follow one another in the same block section
options.C: Trains are worked only by pilot engines
options.D: Block stations are not required at all

e: Under the Absolute Block System, only one train is allowed to be in a block section between two block stations at a time.

q: A 'Caution Order' issued to a loco pilot serves to:

options.A: Cancel the running of a train
options.B: Intimate a change in the time-table
options.C: Inform him about the speed restrictions and special precautions to be observed on the section ahead
options.D: Order attachment of an extra coach to the train

e: A Caution Order informs the loco pilot about the speed restrictions and special precautions to be observed on the section ahead.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The designation of the 'Guard' of a train has been changed to 'Train Manager'.
2. 'Running rooms' at stations are rest facilities provided for passengers waiting for connecting trains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Guard of a train has been redesignated as Train Manager, while running rooms are rest facilities for running staff like drivers and guards, not for passengers.

q: Air-conditioned travel on Indian Railways began in 1936, when an air-conditioned coach was first provided on the:
e: Air-conditioned travel on Indian Railways began in 1936, when the first air-conditioned coach was provided on the Frontier Mail.

q: The first electric suburban train service in Madras (Chennai), started in 1931, ran between:
e: The first electric suburban train service in Madras started in 1931 between Madras Beach and Tambaram.

q: The 'Fairy Queen', among the world's oldest working steam locomotives, was built in the year:
e: The Fairy Queen, one of the world's oldest working steam locomotives, preserved in India, was built in 1855.

q: India's first solar-powered train, introduced in 2017, ran between:
e: India's first solar-powered train, a DEMU fitted with rooftop solar panels, was introduced in 2017 between Delhi Sarai Rohilla and Farukhnagar.

q: The 'Namo Bharat' rapid rail trains operate on which corridor?
e: The Namo Bharat rapid rail trains operate on the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut regional rapid transit corridor.

q: The name 'Garib Rath' of the Garib Rath Express trains literally means:
e: Garib Rath literally means chariot of the poor, as these trains provide affordable fully air-conditioned travel.

q: The word 'Duronto', in the name Duronto Express, is a Bengali word which means:
e: Duronto is a Bengali word meaning restless; Duronto Expresses are long-distance point-to-point trains with very few stops.

q: 'Deen Dayalu' coaches introduced in long-distance trains are meant primarily for:
e: Deen Dayalu coaches are improved unreserved general class coaches with better seating and amenities, introduced in long-distance trains.

q: 'Anubhuti' coaches of Indian Railways are:

options.C: Parcel vans attached to mail trains
options.D: Luxury air-conditioned coaches with aircraft-like amenities, provided in Shatabdi trains

e: Anubhuti coaches are luxury air-conditioned coaches with aircraft-like amenities provided in Shatabdi Express trains.

q: Chennai Central railway station has been renamed in honour of the former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu:
e: Chennai Central station has been renamed after Dr. M. G. Ramachandran, the former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu.

q: The Godavari Arch Bridge near Rajahmundry is built across the river:
e: The Godavari Arch Bridge near Rajahmundry, one of the longest span concrete arch bridges in Asia, is built across the Godavari river.

q: The Nehru Setu, one of the longest railway bridges in India, located near Dehri-on-Sone in Bihar, spans the river:
e: The Nehru Setu near Dehri-on-Sone in Bihar spans the Son river and is one of the longest railway bridges in India.

q: In the context of railway staff working hours, 'HOER' stands for:
e: HOER stands for Hours of Employment Regulations, which govern the hours of work and periods of rest of railway staff.

q: The Railway Property (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1966 deals with:
e: The Railway Property (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1966 provides punishment for unlawful possession of railway property.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mughalsarai Junction has been renamed as Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction.
2. Allahabad Junction has been renamed as Prayagraj Junction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Mughalsarai Junction has been renamed Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction, and Allahabad Junction has been renamed Prayagraj Junction.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Shramik Special' trains were run in 2020 to carry stranded migrant workers to their home States during the COVID-19 lockdown.
2. 'Clone' trains were introduced exclusively for the movement of freight traffic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: Shramik Special trains ran in 2020 for stranded migrant workers, while clone trains are duplicate passenger trains run for waitlisted passengers, not for freight.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. IREPS is the e-procurement system of Indian Railways used for online tendering.
2. 'Railnet' is the in-house data communication network (intranet) of Indian Railways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: IREPS is the e-procurement system of Indian Railways for online tendering, and Railnet is its in-house intranet data communication network.

q: The 'UTS on Mobile' application of Indian Railways is used for booking:
e: The UTS on Mobile application of Indian Railways is used for booking unreserved general tickets through a mobile phone.

q: A 'turntable' provided in a locomotive shed is used for:

options.A: Turning the locomotive to face the required direction

e: A turntable in a locomotive shed is a rotating platform used for turning the locomotive to face the required direction.

q: The Ranchi division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Ranchi division of Indian Railways belongs to South Eastern Railway.

q: The Public Accounts Committee of the Indian Parliament consists of how many members?
e: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament consists of 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

q: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be elected as a member of the Rajya Sabha is:
e: The minimum age prescribed for election to the Rajya Sabha is 30 years, as laid down in Article 84 of the Constitution.

q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha, if not returned by the Rajya Sabha with its recommendations, is deemed to have been passed by both Houses after the expiry of:
e: A Money Bill is deemed passed by both Houses if the Rajya Sabha does not return it with recommendations within 14 days.

q: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by the:

options.C: Chief Justice of the High Court of the State
options.D: Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly

e: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of that State under Article 159.

q: The Chief Election Commissioner of India can be removed from office:

options.A: By the President at his pleasure
options.B: In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court
options.C: By a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha alone
options.D: On the advice of the Union Council of Ministers

e: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

q: At present, the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India lists how many languages?
e: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution at present lists 22 languages.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. President's Rule can be imposed in a State under Article 356 of the Constitution.
2. The total period for which President's Rule can remain in force in a State cannot exceed three years.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: President's Rule is imposed under Article 356, and its total period cannot exceed three years.

q: The feature of 'single citizenship' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The feature of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of the United Kingdom.

q: The elections to the Panchayats in a State are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of:
e: Elections to the Panchayats are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of the State Election Commission under Article 243K.

q: The 'Drain of Wealth' theory, explaining the economic exploitation of India under British rule, was propounded by:
e: The Drain of Wealth theory was propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji, who argued that India's wealth was being drained to Britain under colonial rule.

q: Vasco da Gama, the Portuguese explorer, reached Calicut on the Malabar coast of India in the year:
e: Vasco da Gama, the Portuguese explorer, reached Calicut on the Malabar coast in 1498, discovering the sea route from Europe to India.

q: The last Mughal emperor of India was:
e: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor; he was deposed after the Revolt of 1857 and exiled to Rangoon.

q: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Kanpur was led by:
e: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Kanpur was led by Nana Saheb, the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II.

q: The Indian National Congress declared 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) as its goal at its session held in 1929 at:
e: The Congress declared Purna Swaraj, or complete independence, as its goal at its Lahore session of 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

q: The call of 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement of 1942 was given by:
e: The call of Do or Die was given by Mahatma Gandhi at the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

q: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was declared by:
e: The declaration Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it was made by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

q: 'Jana Gana Mana' was adopted as the National Anthem of India on:
e: Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950 by the Constituent Assembly.

q: The words 'Satyameva Jayate', inscribed below the National Emblem of India, have been taken from the:
e: The words Satyameva Jayate, inscribed below the National Emblem, have been taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

q: The river Godavari originates at:
e: The river Godavari originates at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra, in the Brahmagiri hills.

q: The McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and:
e: The McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector.

q: The rivers Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet to form the Ganga at:
e: The rivers Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag in Uttarakhand, and their combined stream is known as the Ganga.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Khadar is the new alluvial soil found in the flood plains, which is renewed almost every year.
2. Bangar is the old alluvial soil, and it is more fertile than Khadar because it is renewed by floods every year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: Khadar is the new alluvial soil of the flood plains renewed almost every year, while Bangar is the older alluvium and is less fertile, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Which place in India receives the highest rainfall?
e: Mawsynram in Meghalaya receives the highest rainfall in India, even more than nearby Cherrapunji.

q: The southernmost point of the territory of India is:
e: Indira Point, on Great Nicobar Island, is the southernmost point of the territory of India.

q: Barren Island, the only active volcano in India, is located in the:
e: Barren Island, the only active volcano in India, is located in the Andaman Sea, east of the Andaman Islands.

q: The full form of NITI Aayog is:

options.A: National Institute for Training of India

e: NITI Aayog stands for National Institution for Transforming India. It was set up on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission as the Government of India's policy think tank.

q: The First Five-Year Plan of India was based on the model developed by:
e: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which links growth to savings and capital formation. The Mahalanobis model was used only from the Second Plan.

q: The World Trade Organisation (WTO), which replaced the GATT, came into existence in the year:
e: The WTO came into existence on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the GATT as the body governing world trade rules.

q: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is located at:
e: The Asian Development Bank has its headquarters at Manila, the capital of the Philippines, where it has been based since its establishment in 1966.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India?
e: Dr. Verghese Kurien is called the Father of the White Revolution for leading Operation Flood, which made India the world's largest milk producer.

q: The 'Silver Revolution' in India is associated with a rapid increase in the production of:
e: The Silver Revolution refers to the rapid rise in egg (poultry) production in India, as against the White Revolution for milk and the Blue Revolution for fish.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Banking and insurance services belong to the secondary sector of the economy.
2. Manufacturing industries belong to the secondary sector of the economy.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: banking and insurance are services and belong to the tertiary sector. Statement 2 is correct: manufacturing, which converts raw materials into finished goods, is the secondary sector.

q: The SI unit of frequency is the:
e: Frequency is measured in cycles per second, and its SI unit is the hertz. The newton measures force, the pascal pressure and the joule energy.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mercury is the only metal which is in liquid state at room temperature.
2. Bromine is the only non-metal which is in liquid state at room temperature.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, and bromine is the only non-metal found liquid at room temperature.

q: Halley's Comet, visible from the Earth, appears after an interval of about:
e: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of about 76 years, so it becomes visible from the Earth roughly once in every 76 years.

q: The ozone layer, which absorbs the harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun, is present in the:
e: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, the layer of the atmosphere above the troposphere, and it absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In plants, the xylem tissue transports water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves.
2. The phloem tissue transports the food prepared by the leaves to the other parts of the plant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots to the leaves, while phloem distributes the food made in the leaves to the rest of the plant.

q: Which gland of the human body is known as the 'master gland'?
e: The pituitary gland is called the master gland because its hormones control the working of most other endocrine glands of the body.

q: The vaccine for rabies was developed by:
e: Louis Pasteur developed the vaccine against rabies. Edward Jenner is associated with the smallpox vaccine and Alexander Fleming with the discovery of penicillin.

q: The great Sanskrit epic 'Mahabharata' is traditionally believed to have been composed by:
e: The Mahabharata is traditionally attributed to Maharishi Ved Vyasa, while the Ramayana is attributed to Valmiki.

q: The book 'Das Kapital', a critique of political economy, was authored by:
e: Das Kapital, the famous critique of political economy and capitalism, was written by Karl Marx; its first volume appeared in 1867.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. All the Nobel Prizes, except the Peace Prize, are presented at Stockholm in Sweden.
2. The Nobel Peace Prize is presented at Oslo in Norway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct. All Nobel Prizes except the Peace Prize are presented at Stockholm in Sweden, while the Nobel Peace Prize is presented at Oslo in Norway.

q: The first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award was:
e: Devika Rani, the leading actress of early Indian cinema, was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award when it was instituted in 1969.

q: The first Indian to become a Grandmaster in chess was:
e: Viswanathan Anand became India's first chess Grandmaster in 1988, paving the way for the country's later strength in world chess.

q: Children's Day in India is celebrated every year on:
e: Children's Day is celebrated on 14 November, the birth anniversary of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, who was fondly called Chacha Nehru by children.

q: The Ambala division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: Ambala division, covering parts of Haryana, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh, is one of the divisions of the Northern Railway, headquartered at New Delhi.

q: The Prayagraj division (formerly Allahabad division) is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Prayagraj division (earlier Allahabad division) is administered by the North Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Prayagraj itself.

q: The Mumbai Central division is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Mumbai Central division is a division of the Western Railway, which is headquartered at Churchgate, Mumbai.

q: The Solapur division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Solapur division, covering parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, belongs to the Central Railway, headquartered at Mumbai CSMT.

q: The Salem division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Salem division, formed in 2007, is a part of the Southern Railway, whose headquarters is at Chennai.

q: The Tinsukia division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Tinsukia division in upper Assam is administered by the Northeast Frontier Railway, headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati.

q: The Chakradharpur division is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Chakradharpur division, a major freight-loading division of Jharkhand and Odisha region, is a part of the South Eastern Railway.

q: The Khurda Road division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Khurda Road division in Odisha belongs to the East Coast Railway, which is headquartered at Bhubaneswar.

q: 'Baroda House', located near India Gate in New Delhi, houses the headquarters of:
e: Baroda House, near India Gate in New Delhi, is the headquarters building of the Northern Railway, the largest zonal railway.

q: The Banaras Locomotive Works (earlier Diesel Locomotive Works) at Varanasi was set up in technical collaboration with:
e: The Diesel Locomotive Works at Varanasi (now Banaras Locomotive Works) was set up in collaboration with ALCO (American Locomotive Company) of the USA for making diesel locomotives.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) was incorporated in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the dedicated financing arm of Indian Railways, was incorporated in December 1986.

q: The Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) was incorporated in the year:
e: The Container Corporation of India (CONCOR), which operates container terminals and container trains, was incorporated in 1988.

q: The full form of CORE, the organisation headquartered at Prayagraj, is:
e: CORE stands for Central Organisation for Railway Electrification. Headquartered at Prayagraj, it executes railway electrification projects across the country.

q: The Railway Protection Force was conferred the status of an 'Armed Force of the Union' in the year:
e: The Railway Protection Force was conferred the status of an Armed Force of the Union in 1985 through an amendment of the RPF Act.

q: The 'Science Express' run on Indian Railways was a special train meant for:

options.A: A mobile science exhibition to create scientific awareness among students and the public
options.C: Transporting scientific equipment to research stations

e: The Science Express was a specially designed mobile exhibition train that toured the country to promote scientific awareness among students and the general public.

q: The Habibganj railway station of Bhopal, redeveloped as a world-class station, has been renamed as:
e: Bhopal's Habibganj station, redeveloped as a world-class station, was renamed Rani Kamalapati station after the legendary Gond queen of Bhopal.

q: The Kerala Express runs between New Delhi and:
e: The Kerala Express is a daily train running between New Delhi and Thiruvananthapuram Central, covering the length of Kerala.

q: The Goa Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin (Delhi) and:
e: The Goa Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi and Vasco da Gama, the principal railhead for Goa.

q: The Kaveri Express runs between:
e: The Kaveri Express runs between Chennai Central and Mysuru, taking its name from the river Kaveri (Cauvery).

q: The Rockfort Express runs between Chennai Egmore and:
e: The Rockfort Express runs between Chennai Egmore and Tiruchchirappalli, and is named after the famous Rockfort temple of Trichy.

q: 'Rajya Rani' Express trains of Indian Railways were introduced to:

options.B: Connect the State capital with other important towns and district centres of the State
options.C: Provide luxury travel to tourists in royal States
options.D: Carry State Government officials on tour

e: Rajya Rani Express trains were introduced to connect the State capital with other important towns and district headquarters within the same State.

q: 'Suvidha' Express trains of Indian Railways are characterised by:

options.B: Halt at every station on the route
options.C: Dynamic fare pricing, under which fares rise with increasing demand

e: Suvidha Express trains work on dynamic fare pricing, under which the fare rises as seats fill up and demand increases, similar to airline pricing.

q: The Kamayani Express derives its name from:

options.B: The celebrated Hindi epic poem 'Kamayani' of Jaishankar Prasad
options.D: A hill station of Madhya Pradesh

e: The Kamayani Express is named after Kamayani, the celebrated Hindi epic poem written by the Chhayavad poet Jaishankar Prasad.

q: The Vaigai Express, running between Chennai Egmore and Madurai, is named after:

options.D: The river Vaigai which flows through Madurai

e: The Vaigai Express is named after the river Vaigai, which flows through Madurai, the train's destination from Chennai Egmore.

q: The approximate length of the Konkan Railway route, from Roha to Thokur, is:
e: The Konkan Railway, running along the west coast from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangaluru, has a route length of about 741 km.

q: The approximate length of the Bogibeel rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra is:
e: The Bogibeel bridge over the Brahmaputra in Assam, the longest rail-cum-road bridge in India, is about 4.94 km long.

q: The platform at Shri Siddharoodha Swamiji station, Hubballi, the longest railway platform in the world, is approximately:
e: The platform at Hubballi's Shri Siddharoodha Swamiji station, about 1,507 metres long, is recognised as the longest railway platform in the world.

q: The approximate length of the Trans-Siberian Railway, the longest railway line in the world, is:
e: The Trans-Siberian Railway between Moscow and Vladivostok, about 9,289 km long, is the longest railway line in the world.

q: The longest railway tunnel in the world, the Gotthard Base Tunnel, is located in:
e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel, the longest railway tunnel in the world at about 57 km, passes under the Alps in Switzerland.

q: The Channel Tunnel, an undersea rail tunnel, connects:
e: The Channel Tunnel is an undersea rail tunnel beneath the English Channel connecting England (Folkestone) with France (Calais).
